name: media-frame
description:
The BRAND treatment of a cropped picture — the part `.frame` does not do.

`.frame` is a layout primitive and it already owns the mechanics: an aspect ratio, `overflow: hidden`, and a child stretched to fill with `object-fit: cover`. The first version of this unit re-declared all of that, which is a duplicate wearing a different name — the name check was done and the CAPABILITY check was not, and that is the more useful of the two.

What is left is genuinely brand: the corner, the ground behind a slow image, the shaped crops (arch, lens), the paper edge that hides a border printed into the file, and a caption placed under the frame rather than inside it.
surfaceNote: every illustration on the marketing pages

media.$description: The picture. A `media` unit, or a bare img/video.

caption.$description: An optional note, rendered UNDER the frame.

base.$description:
The figure. It carries no crop mechanics — `.frame` on the crop part does that — only the block it occupies and its own container, which every composite here declares so a `cqi` inside measures the frame.

`position: relative` because a frame is a positioning context for anything laid OVER the picture. Dropping it when the crop mechanics moved to `.frame` let an absolutely-positioned overlay escape to the page — it went from 1012px inside the figure to 1280px across the viewport, which a screenshot of the top of the page would not have shown.

shape.$description: The outline. `band` is the default and needs no class.

arch.$description: Flat foot, domed head — a doorway. Written as an ELLIPSE, so a wide frame keeps a shallow sweep instead of the half-circle two equal corner radii would force.

lens.$description: No flat edge at all — what a question looks like.

ratio.$description: Follow the FILE. A frame whose ratio disagrees with its image makes `object-fit: cover` throw the difference away, which is how a 16:9 illustration ends up cropped to a strip.

fill.$description: No ratio of its own — it takes the height of whatever it sits beside.

edge.$description:
A drawn border around the crop.

The illustrations in this brand carry a white frame baked into their pixels, and a shaped crop cuts that frame at an angle — thick down one side, gone at the dome. `paper` draws an EVEN one instead, in the page's own ground, outside the clip so the shape stays clean. Pair it with `inset` on the media, which pushes the baked edge out of the crop.

inset.$description: Scale the media past its own baked edge, so a frame printed into the file lands outside the crop rather than being sliced by it.

crop.$description: The clipping box. Wears `.frame` for the mechanics and this for the brand's corner and ground.

caption.$description: UNDER the frame, never over it: inside a curved crop a caption is sliced mid-word by the very shape it describes.

a11y.note: Decorative art takes `alt=""` and the frame `aria-hidden`; art that carries meaning describes it in `alt` and keeps the caption for the credit.
